title: Replying to @Alex   @Brandon Powers @sweaty oracle  #nexttonormal #br...
transcript: so I've had a few people ask me what I thought of the Next to Normal Proshot particularly because I posted kind of a lukewarm review of the show when I saw it in London but just to be clear like I I did really like the production I was just a little surprised by the hype for it because it didn't seem that different to me from the original one thing that definitely has changed is that I appreciated the performances more particularly Eleanor Worthington-Cox and Jack Wolfe who I I liked but I just didn't really get the hype when I saw the show in the West End but now I feel like I get the hype and I don't know if that's because I was seeing it for a second time so I could just appreciate it a little more or if it's because the Proshot gave me a much closer look because I was sitting in literally the back row of the balcony when I saw it in London but as far as the original question of like did this improve upon the original? and like has my opinion changed on that seeing the Proshot? I will say first of all I don't think the proshot changed my opinion if anything I think time and hearing other people's perspectives might have changed my opinion slightly even then though I'm I'm not totally sure I watched a couple videos about this I watched sweaty Oracle's video and I watched Brendon Powers’ video and they they kind of disagree with each other but I think they both raise good points that in both cases made me realize that maybe I had underestimated the degree of difference between the two productions whether that is positive or negative one thing I brought up in my original video that sweaty Oracle also brings up is the small change at the end which I do think significantly reframes the message that we walk away from the show with but I do still think there are ways in which the material kind of sensationalizes and sort of soap operaifies mentaI iIIness and you know as much as I adore the material I cannot tell you how much I adore this show I think there are problems with it that were not limited to Michael Greif’s direction of the original production but one of the other realizations that I came to is that you know I I may have underplayed this a little bit but I saw the original production when I was quite young but I saw it four times I saw it on Broadway once and on tour three times when it came to my hometown and I do actually think that considering my age I had a pretty good grapple on the material and the various layers to it but because of that I might have been slightly over-estimating my ability at the time to not necessarily remember I remember the production pretty well but I might not have been equipped to accurately assess and internalize the little nuanced ways in which the directorial vision was contributing to the overall tone of the show and the interpretation of the subject matter so it's possible that this production was a lot more mature and nuanced and I just didn't really notice because I am a lot more mature and nuanced and I just assumed it was me and not the production in any case though the short answer to this question (which we’re too late for that) but the short answer is: proshot good production good next to normal good and I'm so excited that people are excited about it again
